title: Batch rename preview does not update as the user types
reasoning: The find and replace fields only set target/action, while the per-keystroke controlTextDidChange hook is never wired as either field's delegate. NSTextField actions fire on commit/end editing, so the preview table and Rename enabled state can stay stale while text is being typed.
reproduction: Open batch rename, type a find pattern that should change filenames, and observe that the preview and Rename button do not update until the field commits rather than on each edit.
recommendation: Assign findField.delegate and replaceField.delegate to self, or otherwise explicitly subscribe to text-change notifications for both fields, so updatePreview runs for each edit.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked UI tests cover batch rename field editing or Rename button enablement.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an AppKit controller test that sends text-change notifications for the find and replace fields and asserts previewNames and renameButton.isEnabled update immediately.
minimumFixScope: Wire BatchRenameViewController text fields to the existing NSTextFieldDelegate path.

history.reasoning: The original path still exists, but the evidence has changed. In Grove/Controllers/BatchRenameViewController.swift, setupUI now assigns findField.delegate = self at line 51 and replaceField.delegate = self at line 62, while controlTextDidChange at lines 249-252 still calls updatePreview(). That wires both text fields to the per-keystroke NSTextFieldDelegate path the finding said was missing, so the stale preview/rename-button issue is fixed in current code. I found no BatchRename regression tests in GroveTests.
